questions.q: What is PMD's relationship to Salesforce Code Analyzer?
options: PMD is a competitor product unrelated to Code Analyzer
PMD only scans JavaScript, never Apex
PMD is one of the underlying engines Code Analyzer bundles, specifically configured with rules for Apex and Visualforce
PMD replaced Code Analyzer entirely and the latter no longer exists
questions.explain: Code Analyzer runs multiple engines, and PMD is the one doing most of the actual rule-checking for Apex and Visualforce by default.

questions.q: What does the --target flag on sf code-analyzer run control?
options: A glob pattern selecting which files get scanned
Which Salesforce org the scan authenticates to
The minimum Apex code coverage percentage
Whether Apex tests run before the scan
questions.explain: --target takes a glob pattern (e.g. force-app/**/*.cls) that scopes the scan to specific files rather than the whole repository.

questions.q: Where would a team persistently configure which PMD languages (e.g. adding JavaScript for LWC) are active, instead of passing it as a flag every run?
options: sfdx-project.json
The GitHub Actions secrets store
The quiz.json file
A code-analyzer.yml file at the project root, under the pmd engine's rule_languages setting
questions.explain: code-analyzer.yml is the persistent project-level configuration file; adding rule_languages under its pmd section enables additional languages consistently across every run.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what kinds of problems do PMD's bundled Apex rules catch?
options: Only spelling mistakes in comments
Only missing semicolons
Concrete, common problems like empty catch blocks that silently swallow exceptions, unused variables, overly complex methods, and patterns preceding SOQL injection
Only Apex test coverage percentages
questions.explain: PMD's bundled Apex/Visualforce rules target real, common code-quality and security-adjacent problems, not just cosmetic style issues.

questions.q: What does this lesson say actually turns a static analysis command into a real quality gate, rather than just a report generator?
options: Running it with --target set to the whole repository
Simply having PMD installed on the CI runner
Writing the output to an HTML file instead of JSON
Configuring it so the command itself exits non-zero once a finding at or above a chosen severity appears, which GitHub Actions then uses to fail the step and block a required check
questions.explain: A gate requires the step to actually fail on a serious-enough finding -- the non-zero exit is what GitHub Actions reads to mark the check failed and, with branch protection, block the merge.
